events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.69 (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so the fare model is per-unit metered distance and the route-deviation remedy is RD-2's partial refund of the unexcused extra kilometres. The record settles the measurement: actual 13.2 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, with one off-route segment 22:58–23:05 driving 3.82 km where the optimal route covers 1.91 km, adding 1.91 km [F1][F2][F3], and the fare record confirms the billed excess: $3.54 = 2.51 km × $1.4102/km, that rate being this trip's distance fare over distance km [F4][F6].

The only excuse the driver offers is congestion: his post-trip statement says "Central Expressway was crawling, so I went round it" [F10]. RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident fact on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, reported before the detour; the record has none [F14], and RD-4(b) is explicit that a speed band alone does not exempt — so the speed band 1 reading on Central Expressway, and the band 4 readings on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Kent Ridge Road, cannot carry an exemption here [F11][F12][F13][RD-4]. Nothing establishes that the replaced stretch was the Central Expressway at all: the fact table carries no road names for the driven path, and the only place-name link comes from the driver's own statement, which is a claim, not consent [F10][RD-5].

RD-5 therefore fails at consent, not merely at scope: the complete chat record is two timestamped messages, the rider announcing his position and the driver his arrival, both sent at 22:43, well before the segment started at 22:58 — neither is an agreement to any route [F7][F8][F9]. The driver's assertion that "any driver would have done the same" appears only in his statement written after the trip, and a driver's claim of agreement that lives only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment counts [RD-5]. There was also no rider-requested stop: no rider message named any place the car stopped at, so RD-3(a) gives no relief [F7][F8][F9][RD-3].

Amount: the segment is the only off-route fact, it is not exempt, and its extra distance is 1.91 km [F3]. At this trip's rate, $18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = $1.4102/km; 1.91 km × $1.4102/km = $2.6935, rounded to $2.69 [F4][F6][RD-2]. This is well within the fare record's own excess-distance figure of $3.54 for 2.51 km, the remainder being unmatched corridor wobble that RD-2 does not refund [F4][RD-2]. Because RD-6 requires at least one prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld (route: 0) [F17], no account flag follows [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint in full. The complaint alleges a longer route and an unasked-for change, not dangerous driving; the messages are logistics (kerb position, car description) and the statement is a routing justification. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so the screen is clean [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured [F3], the fare rate is recorded [F4][F6], and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9], so every element this ruling needs is settled.

The trip log showed 1.91 km of extra distance on your RydeTAXI ride that wasn't justified — the route you were driven covered more ground than the fastest reasonable route for that stretch. We checked the driver's explanation about traffic and the messages exchanged on the trip; nothing in them showed you agreed to that route or that a reported traffic incident forced it.

The voucher covers just the unexplained distance, not the full fare difference. Your account isn't flagged, so nothing changes for future rides.

DRIVER: We've reviewed this trip and are applying a $2.69 Ryde voucher to the rider, for 1.91 km of extra distance on the route driven.

The decision rested on two points: no traffic incident was reported on the road you would otherwise have taken, before you detoured, and the ride chat contains no rider agreement to that route. Congestion alone doesn't qualify as an excuse.

This is a fare adjustment only. No account flag or penalty follows, since you have no prior upheld route disputes on record. No further action is needed from you.

notices.text:
We've reviewed your dispute and will refund $2.69 as a Ryde voucher on your account.

The trip log showed 1.91 km of extra distance on your RydeTAXI ride that wasn't justified — the route you were driven covered more ground than the fastest reasonable route for that stretch. We checked the driver's explanation about traffic and the messages exchanged on the trip; nothing in them showed you agreed to that route or that a reported traffic incident forced it.

The voucher covers just the unexplained distance, not the full fare difference. Your account isn't flagged, so nothing changes for future rides.

We've reviewed this trip and are applying a $2.69 Ryde voucher to the rider, for 1.91 km of extra distance on the route driven.
